claims.statement: Atlas issues a Bearer access token in exchange for a service account's client ID and secret at POST https://cloud.mongodb.com/api/oauth/token; the token is reusable and valid for 1 hour (3600 seconds).

sources.supports: info.description: 'returns a Bearer token that is reusable and valid for 1 hour (3600 seconds)'

claims.statement: The access token is sent in the Authorization header with the Bearer scheme to Atlas Administration API endpoints.
When an organization requires an IP access list, the token can be created from any address but the API call that uses it must come from an allowed address.

sources.supports: info.description: 'the token can be created from any IP address, but the API call that uses the token must originate from an allowed IP.'

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Existence, lifetime and carrier only; no format claim. A bare value cannot be attributed to this family without context.

openQuestions.question: What does the access token look like (prefix, encoding, length, whether it is a JSON Web Token)? None of the pages read describes the token's form, so a bare token value cannot be attributed to Atlas from its shape. A provider statement is needed.
How is a token revoked before expiry? The documentation index names a revoke procedure (revoke-oauth2-token-atlas) that was not read.
